title: Book One · Chapter 121: Three Dry Pencils
story:
The used table has a grey top and one dark foot. Ronan looks at the dark foot. “That foot has a sock,” he says.

“That is the right size,” Mr Qiu says.

Mr Sun stands at his work counter. He reads the numbers on the paper. Then he looks at Dad.

“The back edge is rough. It needs some work.”

“I saw it,” Dad says. “I can do that after this job.”

“After that job, yes. The man is coming for it at five.”

Ronan stands well away from the tools. He has come with Mum. He will help carry the small empty boxes home. Mr Qiu will pay for the table himself. Adults will move it.

“Does the dark foot cost extra?” Ronan asks.

Mr Sun looks at him. “That is its best foot.”

Mr Qiu pays the price they agree on. He counts the money slowly. Ronan turns away. Mr Qiu can pay by himself. Ronan can wait beside Mum. Ronan waits beside Mum until they have finished.

At the green gate, Mrs Lan looks at their marks. The table fits between them. The gate opens. Mum walks through with the washing basket. Nothing hits it.

“Your washing is our first customer,” Mr Qiu says.

“It has no money,” Mum tells him.

The next morning, Mr Qiu puts three pencil boxes on the table. He adds a stack of dry notebooks and a little cup for coins. The rest stays packed away. The two wooden crates are empty now. Mr Qiu takes them back to his own place that evening.

Ronan wants to write OPEN on a large sheet.

“We have a sign,” Mr Qiu says.

He takes a small old board from his bag. His name is on it. The paint has worn away near one corner.

“Could I make a new one?”

“You could help me clean this one.”

They wipe it with a nearly dry cloth. The dirt comes off. Now they can read the name. Ronan holds the board while Mr Qiu sets it by the notebooks.

A woman stops outside the gate. She looks through it, then looks up the street.

“I thought you were closed.”

“My other place is closed,” Mr Qiu says. “My pencils are working here.”

She buys three. Ronan watches him put them in a narrow paper bag. She only buys three pencils. Ronan watches her take the bag. Mr Qiu can sell things again. Ronan grins at him across the table.

Mrs Lan comes out after the woman leaves. She moves one box a little.

“This corner must stay behind the line.”

“It will,” Mr Qiu says.

At supper Ronan tells Dad about the sale. Dad asks, “Does the table stand firm?”

“Very firm. Even with three pencils gone.”

Dad puts his spoon down and laughs.

Rain begins again before bed. Ronan looks through the window. The table is empty. All the stock is in small closed boxes on the checked high shelf. Mrs Lan's front room is clear for her sister.

The roof at the old stall still needs work. But tonight the pencils are dry. Mr Qiu can open his table again tomorrow.

Ronan moves his own drawing paper away from the window. One corner was against the wall. He feels it with his thumb. It is cool but dry. He puts the stack flat under his book. Then he leaves the window open just a little, as Mum asks. Mum wants some fresh air in the room. Ronan checks the paper by the window. Rain cannot reach it now.

---

重点表达：rough＝粗糙的；stock＝待售物品；stands firm＝站得稳。

情节提示：counter＝柜台；notebook＝笔记本；worn away＝磨损脱落。

理解：1. 谁付钱买了旧桌子？2. 夜里文具放在哪里？
